correctness.rationale: For nonzero \(A=EN\), a nontrivial idempotent must project onto \(\operatorname{im}A\). Choosing a complement gives \(E=\mathrm{diag}(1,0)\), \(A=\begin{pmatrix}t&s\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\), and every completion \(N=\begin{pmatrix}t&s\\x&y\end{pmatrix}\) is nilpotent exactly when \(y=-t\) and \(sx=-t^2\). If \(t=0\), every one of the \(q\) complements works uniquely plus \(E=I\), giving \(q+1\); if \(t\ne0\), exactly the complement \(\ker A\) fails, giving \(q-1\). The zero fiber is \(q^2+1+q^2(q+1)=q^3+2q^2+1\). Transposition transfers EN fibers of \(A\) to NI fibers of \(A^T\), and the formula depends only on zero/trace/determinant class. A fresh exhaustive replay over prime fields \(q=2,3,5\) matched every target.
correctness.risk: The general proof uses only dimension-two finite-field line geometry; no extrapolation to higher dimensions or non-field local rings is made.

final_claim: For every prime power \(q\) and \(A\in M_2(\mathbb F_q)\), the ordered idempotent--nilpotent and nilpotent--idempotent factorization fibers have the common exact sizes \(q^3+2q^2+1\) at zero, \(q+1\) at each nonzero nilpotent, \(q-1\) at each nonnilpotent singular matrix, and \(0\) at invertible matrices.
limitations: Only \(M_2(\mathbb F_q)\) and one idempotent/one nilpotent factor are classified.
